messages:
elaine: opened a small PR to update model cards + catalog guidance for the quantization profile rename and deprecation plan. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/13321
sam: nice. can you summarize what is changing in one sentence for the card header? ops will need to point customers to it a lot.
elaine: TL;DR: we are renaming the legacy `cpu-quant` alias to `cpu-quant-stable` and introducing `cpu-quant-experimental` for newer aggressive quant profiles; `cpu-quant` will be deprecated with 30d notice. added that to the top of each affected card.
marco: did quick benches comparing stable vs experimental quant on medium seqs (1k). gist: https://gist.github.com/marco/quant-profile-compare. key numbers pasted in PR.
fiona: runtime asked we add a clear compatibility note: experimental profiles may not be available in all regions or on Dedicated, so docs should state availability and fallback behavior.
rik: from runtime side: also add explicit OOM/capacity guidance: "cpu-quant-stable: recommended up to 4k; cpu-quant-experimental: up to 6k best-effort but may OOM on shared infra; for production >6k use GPU-backed variants or Dedicated."
sam: can we include an example fallback policy that prefers experimental but falls back to stable then gpu if needed? that'll make support answers easier.
elaine: added YAML snippet in the card for the fallback policy:
```yaml
fallbacks:
  - prefer: model-long (gpu)
  - prefer: model-cpu-quant-experimental
  - fallback: model-cpu-quant-stable
  - final-fallback: model-gpu-quant
```
marco: pasted compact perf blurb into PR for both quant profiles at 1k context: "cpu-quant-stable: median 8 tps, p95 14 tps; cpu-quant-experimental: median 12 tps, p95 18 tps (higher variance)."
fiona: added wording about variance: "Experimental profiles trade stability for throughput; expect occasional latency spikes and retries on shared nodes."
elsam: (typo) elaine: also fixed a broken model-variants anchor that link-checker flagged. replaced absolute anchor with canonical `/models/<name>/variants` path and added a redirect frontmatter.
sam: SDK examples: please include both a short Python snippet showing detection of 413/429 and a JS streaming example that shows how to switch to a GPU-backed variant if a 413 occurs.
elaine: added both. Python error handling snippet:
```python
try:
  r = client.generate(model="nebula-7b", prompt=prompt, max_tokens=1000)
except ApiError as e:
  if e.status_code == 413:
    # fallback: switch to long GPU variant or reduce max_tokens
    print("Payload too large; try GPU-backed model or reduce tokens")
```
JS snippet (auto-fallback):
```javascript
let model = 'nebula-7b-cpu-quant-experimental'
try {
  const res = await client.generate({ model, prompt, max_tokens: 1500 })
} catch (err) {
  if (err.status === 413) {
    model = 'nebula-7b-long' // gpu-backed
    const res2 = await client.generate({ model, prompt, max_tokens: 1500 })
  }
}
```
marco: link-checker preview requested: docs-bot please deploy preview when PR opened.
docs-bot: preview deployed for PR 13321: https://deploy.preview.redwood/docs/changes/13321  link-checker: 1 broken link -> /models/nebula-7b#variants (fixed in branch)
fiona: small nit: update the deprecation schedule text to mention the 30-day notice and a migration checklist. customers want steps (find alias, update SDK config, verify in preview).
elaine: added a Migration checklist section with 3 bullets: find uses of `cpu-quant`, replace with `cpu-quant-stable` or `cpu-quant-experimental`, run quick perf tests in preview and validate error handling.
sam: product asks to add a one-line cost guidance: "experimental quant often reduces cost per token but may increase tail latency; benchmark for your workload."
marco: added a tiny CSV and pasted the single-line cost estimate into the card: "rough unit cost: stable ~$0.002/token, experimental ~$0.0016/token (varies by region and load)."
fiona: runtime verified the cost ballpark but asked to add "estimate only" and a pointer to Redwood Optimize for precise suggestions. added that pointer.
elaine: ok to merge once link-checker is green and legal approves the deprecation copy. thanks all for quick iter. :tada:
